Every umbrella at the stop pops open. Except Eli's. In this world, an umbrella only opens if someone is waiting for you to get home.
He shakes it. He bangs it. It stays shut. He checks his phone. No messages. He's lived alone since the spring.
So he walks home. Forty minutes. Soaked to the bone. He tells himself it doesn't matter. Umbrellas are for tourists.
Halfway home, it bursts open on its own.
In his front window, Pepper is waiting. Fourteen years old. Deaf in one ear. He's been sitting at the glass since six.
Hey, old man. You waited for me?
Eli doesn't buy a new umbrella. He doesn't need one.
